claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: An operator merged the finished branch into main after closeout, which makes every checkpoint truthful and the criterion a statement about the run rather than about the tree. This explanation is consistent with the evidence but is not recorded anywhere in the packet, so the criterion still cannot be re-verified.
claimAdjudication.claim: Criterion 7's recorded evidence no longer reproduces from the final tree: the packet's commits, including both recorded close commits, are contained in origin/main.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the branch is ahead of origin/main (it is not), whether the containment applies only to the merge commits (it applies to the packet close commits too), and whether the recorded checkpoints predate the closing commits (they do).
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: A recorded operator merge after closeout, or a closure evidence line re-stated as a time-bound observation instead of a property of the final tree.

findingDetails.evidence: Criterion 7 and the parent scope row say nothing is pushed, and criteria.txt records remote_branches_with_head=0 three times. Today git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main prints 0 5 and origin/main contains HEAD and both recorded close commits.
findingDetails.recommendation: Re-state the criterion's evidence as a time-bound observation with the checkpoint commit, or record the operator merge that moved the branch, so the line can be re-run and interpreted.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Criterion text, parent scope row and recorded evidence line read directly; git probes run read-only and report 0 5, origin/main containment for HEAD and for both close commits.
findingDetails.title: Criterion 7's evidence no longer reproduces: every packet commit is contained in origin/main

noveltyJustification: One finding new to this lineage; no earlier iteration or wave-1 lineage re-ran criterion 7 against live git state.
